claims.text: The quinary alloy and the compared equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Differences in composition among the quinary alloy and its subsets produce variations in stacking-fault energy.
Stacking-fault energy influences whether deformation proceeds by dislocation slip, twinning, or martensitic transformation.
Differences in the activated deformation mechanisms cause differences in strength, ductility, and toughness.
The proposed relationship applies at room temperature and under cryogenic conditions.
Thermomechanical processing is the intervention responsible for changing the stacking-fault-energy mediator across the compared alloys.
The equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets should have lower strength than the quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
The equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets should have lower ductility than the quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
The CrCoNi ternary subset can have better mechanical properties than the CrMnFeCoNi quinary alloy because of its capacity for twinning-controlled deformation.
Grain size and crystal structure may also influence the measured mechanical properties.
The exact quantitative relationship between stacking-fault energy and deformation mechanisms remains uncertain.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule treats lower strength and ductility of all ternary and quaternary subsets as the prediction, whereas the cited same-system evidence states that the CrCoNi ternary has better strength, ductility, and toughness than the quinary baseline and relates this behavior to twinning.
